fields.Core Themes JSON: [{"title": "From Plant Labs to Prison Programs", "body": "Greg entered graduate school in psychology in 1972, when spoon bending parties, pyramid power and the idea that plants could think were in fashion, and his major professor and the professor's psychiatrist wife took him along to them every weekend. None of it could be verified, he says, except one lab test in which a philodendron wired to a physiograph reacted to the student who had secretly torn off its leaf. He went on to run a prison drug treatment program in his early twenties, built a career in criminal psychology, and wrote The Archetype Experience as a follow-up to Carl Jung's book on flying saucers."}, {"title": "Newark's Moon Tracking Earthworks", "body": "Greg calls the Newark Earthworks in Ohio the most extensive geometric earthworks in the world, and recalls Andrew Collins, then living at Avebury, calling them more incredible than Avebury bar the stones. The 20 acre circle and 50 acre octagon, with a flat topped mound at each of the octagon's eight points, were built, he says, to track the moon's 18.61 year cycle so eclipses could be predicted. Greg says ritual artifacts there point to psilocybin use, and where mainstream archaeology reads such rituals as hallucination, the shamans' own accounts, he says, describe manifesting physical spiritual beings inside the earthworks."}, {"title": "Mothman Through John Keel's Eyes", "body": "Greg describes John Keel as unpopular with other ufologists because he saw UFOs as paranormal rather than nuts and bolts, and many of Keel's ideas went into Origins of the Gods. He retells the Mothman affair at Point Pleasant, West Virginia: thirteen months of sightings of a roughly seven foot winged creature with glowing red eyes, reported, he says, by hundreds of people including National Guardsmen, ending when the bridge to Gallipolis, Ohio collapsed around Christmas. He and Andrew Collins met a restaurant owner who described it landing on the roof by her bedroom window, and Keel wrote of a curse laid on the area by the Shawnee chief Cornstalk."}, {"title": "Following the Milky Way to Deneb", "body": "Greg describes a death journey found across North American tribes: the soul leaps to the Orion Nebula, Messier 42, as Orion sinks below the horizon, travels the Milky Way, the path of souls, to a judge that is nearly always a raptor bird, and if it passes goes through Deneb in Cygnus as a portal to the other world. He argues the lore reaches back at least 17,000 years, to when Deneb was the pole star. After engineer Rodney Hale overlaid Cygnus on Giza, Andrew Collins argued the pyramids fit Cygnus better than Orion, while a Cheyenne arrow priest made clear the tribes named stars their own way."}, {"title": "Two Souls and Why the Elite Were Kept", "body": "Greg says Native Americans, like the Egyptians, held that each person has two souls: a life soul that animates the physical body, and a free soul of pure spiritual energy that keeps memory and identity and leaves at death. Most people were cremated, he says, their bones ground down and returned to the soil so the free soul could separate and reincarnate if needed. Chiefs and priests were preserved in stone chambers so their free soul could return to that same body, which Chance suggests is closer to resurrection, a word Greg adopts. Chance's outro ties the two souls to the body intelligence of his biofield work."}]
fields.Intro Paragraph 1: Dr. Gregory Little has spent 50 years documenting UFOs, ancient mounds, and the shamanic contact traditions. His book Origins of the Gods presents plasma as the scientific bridge between transdimensional intelligence and physical manifestation.
fields.Intro Paragraph 2: Covers plasma as self-organizing, potentially conscious beings capable of physical manifestation inside ceremonial geometric earthworks, the Native American Path of Souls cosmology as identical to ancient Egyptian afterlife belief, the Giza pyramid alignment corrected from Orion to Signus by Andrew Collins, Moth Man as a plasma entity, the Newark Ohio lunar earthworks, the two souls concept across Native American and Egyptian traditions, and the shamanic origins of contact with the divine.

fields.Plus Core Themes JSON: [{"title": "The Singularity That Split Into Three Worlds", "body": "Greg lays out the Native American creation account as it survives in very old ethnology books, in which the ethnographers themselves used the word singularity. It begins as a single point of pure spiritual energy carrying a primordial intelligence, which develops two apparently opposing sides like the yin and yang and then splits apart, creating a four dimensional universe. The upper world, symbolized by birds, the sun and the moon, is the force of order and creation. The lower world is entropy and disorder. The physical world sits between them as a two sided mirror where both forces can coexist and balance."}, {"title": "Dirt, Rock and Crystal as Condensed Spirit", "body": "Because the universe started as pure spiritual energy, everything in it stays spiritual, and Greg walks that all the way down into matter. Dirt is the most primordial spiritual energy that exists, which is why the mound builders raised earthworks out of soil rather than stone. Rock is solidified spiritual energy, water is flowing spiritual energy, fire is that energy being released, and crystal is the same energy condensed. Human beings were placed in the middle world to harmonize with order and entropy, which is why land could be occupied and used but never owned, and why every ceremony was tied to star movements."}, {"title": "Plasma as the Fourth State of Matter", "body": "Greg and Andrew Collins argue the genuine UFO and paranormal residue is plasma, an ionized ball of gas wrapped in an electromagnetic shell that pulls in electrons, dust and matter and grows as long as energy keeps feeding it. He cites the British Ministry of Defence Condign report, which concluded that real UFOs are plasmas with probable intelligence, and a 2007 paper in the New Journal of Physics in which seven physicists grew plasmas that formed a double helix down the middle, split, replicated, and let the weaker strands fall apart and die. Feed them enough energy, the physicists wrote, and something living could develop."}, {"title": "Joan of Arc, Swedenborg and the Tricksters", "body": "The same phenomenon runs through recorded history as balls of light. Joan of Arc did not merely hear voices, she stepped inside the light and touched the beings. Emanuel Swedenborg, a respected Swedish scientist, was visited for twenty eight years by a robed figure who promised to open his mind and then flew him to cities on Venus, Mercury and Saturn that Greg is certain were never there. Edgar Cayce's abilities began with an angel in a giant ball of light. Greg's verdict is that these entities lie at first, which is exactly what Carl Jung and the tribes meant by trickster, a test you have to get past."}, {"title": "A Narrow Band of Perception and the Holy Ghost", "body": "Greg treats the eye as hardware, calling the rods and cones biological radio antennas tuned to the exact middle of the electromagnetic spectrum, less than five percent of what is actually there, because creatures able to see all of it could not function. He suspects LSD and other hallucinogens retune those antennas rather than simply inventing images, drawing on his own psychopharmacology lab years and on the Cheyenne arrow priest who saw little blue people move through the walls of his office. His closing speculation is that plasma manifesting individually to each witness is what Christianity has been pointing at with the Holy Ghost."}]
